summary: Istanbul is a tight pick-up-and-deliver game where you move your merchant and assistants around a modular grid of place tiles, leaving assistants behind to trigger repeatable actions while racing to collect rubies for scoring. It plays fast and tense despite the calm theme, with efficient route-planning and light blocking as other players occupy the tiles you need.
praised: Tight, tense action-efficiency puzzle despite simple rules
Modular board gives high replayability and varied setups
Quick turns keep downtime low even at higher player counts
Big Box bundles both expansions plus mini-expansion at good value and improves component quality/insert
criticised: Can feel a bit dry or 'mechanical' thematically
Assistant-placement blocking can occasionally lead to slight kingmaking or bad luck if a needed tile is occupied
Some find the base game a bit light at higher weight expectations; the 5x5 big bazaar mode with more players can drag
Expansions (esp. Letters & Seals) add complexity that not all groups want

interaction.kind: tile/space blocking and light area denial via assistant placement

win_criteria: Most points, one or two sources

scoring.why: The winner is decided almost entirely by rubies collected, with bonus tiles/wheelbarrow upgrades acting as accelerants rather than separate scoring tracks
